newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume doubles, prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume doubles, prices rise.

text.p: Volume on the Istanbul gold exchange more than doubled to 902 kilos on Wednesday from Tuesday's 448 kilos.
Prices rose, but were lower on the bourse when compared with free market levels, which attracted buyers, dealers said.

"Gold prices jumped in the free market in line with the dollar's rise in international and domestic markets. Lower prices on the bourse shifted activity away from the free market to the bourse," a dealer said.
The bulk of the turnover occured in the morning, with 817 kilos, and trade was quieter in the second session as expectations of further price increases faded.
Gold closed at 1,164,000 lira per gram, up from Tuesday's 1,162,200 lira. This reflected the weakness of the lira, which closed at 94,680 per dollar versus Tuesday's 94,450.
Dealers said gold traded as high as 1,166,000 lira on the free market.
In dollar terms, gold gained $0.50 to close at $382.00 an ounce, in line with steadier levels on the world market.
There was no dollar term trade in the afternoon and 89 percent of the daily volume was in lira terms.
Dealers said the uncertain trends on world gold markets kept trade in narrow price ranges on the domestic market.
